title: Observational identification of a sample of likely recent common-envelope events
question: What is the physical nature and evolutionary origin of water fountain (WF) sources, and are they binary systems that have recently undergone common-envelope evolution?

evidence.quote: For eight sources, we used the values obtained from integrating the spectral energy distribution and assuming a luminosity in the range expected for (post-)asymptotic giant branch (AGB) stars (cite: Vickers2015).

evidence.loc: Water-fountain and common-envelope systems formation rates
evidence.quote: We perform a simple analysis using the initial mass function (cite: Kroupa2001) scaled to the recently determined star formation history of the Milky Way (cite: Ruiz-Lara2020).

evidence.loc: Water-fountain and common-envelope systems formation rates
evidence.quote: This relative star formation history is further scaled to the average recent Galactic star formation rate of $1.65\pm0.19$ M$_\odot$ yr$^{-1}$ (cite: Licquia2015).

evidence.loc: Water-fountain and common-envelope systems formation rates
evidence.quote: We then apply the criteria for CE envelope evolution at the late-RGB or early-AGB (a mass ratio $>0.1$ and period $<10$ yr) and the corresponding close binary fractions (cite: Moe2015).

recipe.goal: Extract integrated line fluxes of CO isotopologues
recipe.method: Integrate emission over the velocity range of the slowly expanding outflow (expansion velocity plus 5 km/s turbulence) and correct 12CO for narrow Galactic interstellar emission where present
key_parameters: v_exp = 20 km/s (+ 5 km/s turbulence) for most sources; 23 km/s for IRAS 15103-5754; 25 km/s for IRAS 18450-0148; 65 km/s for IRAS 15445-5449
assumptions: 12C17O and 12C18O lines arise mostly from the slowly expanding envelope component

recipe.goal: Derive 17O/18O isotopic ratios and initial stellar masses
recipe.method: Calculate 17O/18O from integrated 12C17O(1-0) and 12C18O(2-1) line fluxes assuming optically thin LTE emission, then compare to stellar evolution models
assumptions: Optically thin emission, Boltzmann distribution at T_exc = 100 K, and initial solar composition

recipe.goal: Calculate circumstellar H2 gas masses and optical depths
recipe.method: Compute total 12C18O molecules from integrated 12C18O(2-1) flux under optically thin LTE, convert to H2 mass via fractional abundance; for non-detections use 3-sigma 12C18O upper limits and 13CO(2-1) lower limits; compute line-center optical depth
key_parameters: T_exc = 100 K (40 K for 13CO lower limits)
assumptions: Optically thin 12C18O(2-1) emission, box-shaped line profile for optical depth, 16O/18O = 570, X(12C16O) = 3e-4, 12C/13C = 5 for 13CO lower limits

recipe.goal: Estimate outflow ages and average mass-loss rates
recipe.method: Determine outflow age Delta_t = R / v_exp from resolved slow CO outflow sizes (including Band 7 13CO(3-2) maps), H2O maser extents, or ALMA upper limits, and compute Delta_M_H2 / Delta_t = M_H2 * (v_exp / R)
key_parameters: Source radii R and ages Delta_t in Tables 1 and 3
assumptions: Ballistic expansion at the present expansion speed of the low-velocity gas

recipe.goal: Compare Galactic water-fountain formation rate with Common-Envelope event rate
recipe.method: Estimate WF formation rate from 15 known sources and 200 yr lifetime; integrate Kroupa IMF scaled to Milky Way SFH/SFR and close binary fractions (mass ratio > 0.1, period < 10 yr) for stars 0.8-8.0 M_sun
key_parameters: 15 WF sources; WF lifetime ~ 200 yr; Galactic SFR = 1.65 +/- 0.19 M_sun yr^-1; M > 0.95 M_sun; binary mass ratio > 0.1 and period < 10 yr
assumptions: Kroupa IMF, Milky Way SFH of Ruiz-Lara et al. 2020, binary fractions of Moe & Di Stefano 2015
